what: Erie Indemnity is not quite an insurer. It is the management company that runs Erie Insurance Exchange, a policyholder-owned insurer selling car and home cover in the American Midwest and East, and it takes a fixed percentage of the premiums for doing so.
customers: Through independent agents, households and small businesses in about a dozen states.
money: a set percentage of the premiums the Exchange writes
moat: A management agreement with the Exchange that has no expiry and that the Exchange cannot easily replace, which turns insurance premium growth into fee income without taking the underwriting risk.
risks: Revenue depends entirely on one related party, the Exchange, and the fee rate is set by a board
24 times earnings for a business growing with car insurance premiums
If the Exchange underwrites badly, premium growth eventually stalls and so does the fee
opportunities: Revenue grew from $2.6B to $4.1B in four years as car insurance premiums rose sharply
No debt at all, with $380M of cash and a 13.8% net margin
The fee is taken off premiums before claims are paid, so a bad claims year does not hit this company directly
watch: Premium growth at the Exchange and the management fee rate the board sets each year.
